USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Dose adjustment in kidney disease

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 79-year-old man with substantially reduced creatinine clearance is prescribed famotidine for an appropriate indication. His pharmacist recommends reducing the dose or lengthening the interval before treatment begins. Which pharmacokinetic concern most directly supports this adjustment in his case?

  1. Famotidine must be activated by renal bacteria
  2. Reduced filtration increases hepatic first-pass metabolism
  3. The drug is eliminated exclusively in exhaled air
  4. Reduced renal clearance can increase exposure
  5. Kidney disease prevents all intestinal absorption
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Reduced renal clearance can increase exposure

Famotidine is substantially renally eliminated; reduced kidney function raises exposure and adverse-effect risk.

Understanding the options

Reduced renal clearance can increase exposure
Famotidine is substantially renally eliminated; reduced kidney function raises exposure and adverse-effect risk.
Kidney disease prevents all intestinal absorption
Renal disease does not eliminate intestinal absorption.
Famotidine must be activated by renal bacteria
Renal bacterial activation is not required.
Reduced filtration increases hepatic first-pass metabolism
Increased first-pass metabolism is not the relevant mechanism.
The drug is eliminated exclusively in exhaled air
Pulmonary elimination is not its principal route.
